title: Indefinite causal order and quantum coordinates
locators: Def. 1 causal order as sign of proper-time difference (Eq. 2); Def. 2 ICO as s^(1)s^(2)=-1 (Eqs. 5-6, generalization footnote 2); quantum diffeomorphism Eq. (7); operational encoding Eqs. (10)-(12) + Appendix B (Bloch picture Fig. 4); Appendix A.1 Eqs. (13)-(16) delocalized events to superposed metrics; Appendix A.2 Eqs. (17)-(19) superposed metrics to delocalized events via Fermi normal coordinates along gamma0; no-go triple (localized events, definite metric, ICO); Discussion citing refs [53],[54],[24]
assumptions: Superposition of two semi-classical, macroscopically distinguishable metric states alpha|1>|g(1)>+beta|2>|g(2)> (Eq. 3; footnote 1: the Hilbert space of the metric is not constructed, Eq. 3 called 'suggestive'); events defined as worldline coincidences, extended across branches by E_X^(1)=E_X^(2) (Eq. 4); test-particle worldline gamma0 crosses each system worldline exactly once; time orientation fixed by endpoints of gamma0; quantum coordinates = one chart per branch tied by physical events; quantum diffeomorphisms = branch-wise unitary representations U_i of diffeomorphisms (asserted, not explicitly constructed)
conclusion: Whether the causal order between operationally defined events is definite or indefinite, encoded in the product s^(1)s^(2) of branch signs, is invariant under classical diffeomorphisms and under quantum-controlled diffeomorphisms; whether the indefiniteness is due to delocalized events or to a superposition of spacetime metrics is a matter of choice of quantum coordinates (Appendix A maps both directions); no quantum coordinate system realizes simultaneously localized events, a definite metric, and ICO; the sign s is operationally encodable in a qubit register and sigma_x, sigma_y, sigma_z measurements distinguish a coherent superposition of orders from a classical mixture; consequence claimed: the optical quantum switch realizes ICO in the same sense as the gravitational quantum switch, and a realization of ICO does not by itself witness a quantum superposition of spacetime (curvature measurements still distinguish the two)
proof_status: Primary HTML full text read at the stated locators. Invariance of s follows in-paper from branch-wise diffeo-invariance of proper time; Appendix A maps are constructive diffeomorphism arguments read but not reproduced; no-go claim argued and cross-checked by authors against Vilasini-Renner Corollary 1.
dependencies: Diffeomorphism invariance of proper time; Fermi normal coordinates (MTW Sec. 13.6); spin precession as a proper-time clock (Zych et al. 2011; Smith-Ahmadi 2020); QRF program (Giacomini et al. 2019; Vanrietvelde et al. 2020; Kabel et al. 2024); process-matrix and ICO literature via refs [2],[3],[13],[22],[24],[53]-[61]
open_questions: Authors' own open problems: cast quantum-controlled diffeomorphisms in the QRF formalism (explicit U_i and Hilbert space for metric and quantum coordinates); define events for multiple or branch-dependent numbers of crossings; extend beyond superpositions of semi-classical spacetimes; relation to microcausality in AQFT. Ours: the asserted analogy between their invariant s^(1)s^(2) and the preservation of causal order under reversible process-matrix transformations (their refs [53]-[55]) is not derived anywhere in the paper.
relevance: Anchor 1: the relativistic, quantum-coordinate definition of ICO that any temporal-QRF account must be compared against; supplies the invariant s^(1)s^(2) and the localization/metric-superposition trade-off.
limits: ID reused from knowledge/frontier/sources.jsonl (recorded there at discovery depth); this record upgrades it to full-text. The metric Hilbert space and quantum-coordinate formalism remain heuristic; the optical-vs-gravitational claim concerns only the Def. 2 observable; no process-matrix statement is proven here.

title: Measurement events relative to temporal quantum reference frames
version: arXiv:2308.10967v1 (2023-08-21); published as Hausmann, Schmidhuber, Castro-Ruiz, Quantum 9, 1616 (2025), DOI 10.22331/q-2025-01-30-1616 (per ref [25] of arXiv:2603.08845v1)
locators: Sec. II clock model Eqs. (2)-(6) (bounded spectrum sigma=[-E,E], covariant POVM |phi_t>, overlap sinc); Sec. III.1 twirled-observable (TO) approach Eqs. (7)-(11); Sec. III.2 purified-measurement (PM) approach Eqs. (12)-(14); Sec. IV.2.1 non-ideal constraint Eq. (15); Sec. IV.2.2 time-non-local evolution Eq. (16) and Dyson-type solution Eq. (17) with kernel F(t), non-unitarity footnote 2; Sec. IV.2.3 indefinite temporal order Eqs. (19)-(20), Fig. 3; Sec. IV.2.4 Eq. (21) TO internalizes to standard QM; Sec. V Eqs. (22)-(24) discrete-time unitary model; Appendix D Eqs. (55)-(66) TO-PM equivalence for ideal clocks via reduction maps R(tau), R^-1(tau); Appendix F Eq. (106) PM probabilities as time-non-local TO conditional probabilities; Appendix G Eqs. (107)-(115) orthonormal discrete clock basis t_k=k pi/E
assumptions: Clock C with Hilbert space and Hamiltonian H_C=integral over sigma of e|e><e|, sigma=[-E,E]; time measurement by covariant POVM with states |phi_t>; ideal clock = spectrum R with orthogonal |t>; TO: constraint (H_C+H_S)|Psi>=0 with twirled observables; PM: constraint with clock-conditioned measurement interaction K_SA(t), non-ideal generalization Eq. (15); in parts H_S=0; probability rule Eq. (14) whose denominator is trivial only for ideal clocks
conclusion: Authors' claims: for ideal clocks TO and PM give identical multi-time probabilities (proved in Appendix D); for non-ideal clocks they describe operationally distinct situations. TO: unitary evolution, sharp externally chosen order of operations independent of clock resources; internalizable as standard QM with external time. PM: conditional dynamics is time-non-local with memory kernel F(t) (Eq. 16-17), generally non-unitary, with a modified probability rule; with disjoint supports of the two measurement interactions the cross-order term survives, so the temporal order of measurement events is fundamentally limited (indefinite temporal order of PM-defined events), which the authors flag as possibly relevant to process-matrix indefinite causal structure (their refs [32]-[34]); unitarity is restored in a discrete-time PM model (Eqs. 22-24), and the authors state: if best clocks have finite energy spread, measurements are clock-triggered, and unitary evolution is demanded, then time must be discrete
proof_status: Full HTML text read including Appendices A-G; Appendix D equivalence proof inspected stepwise (Eqs. 55-66) and Appendix E perturbative solution inspected, neither numerically reproduced; published peer-reviewed version exists (Quantum 9, 1616, 2025) but was not separately read
dependencies: Page-Wootters formalism; Kuchar criticisms (Kuchar 2011); Giovannetti-Lloyd-Maccone quantum time (2015); Hoehn-Smith-Lock trinity (2021); Smith-Ahmadi interacting clocks (2019); process matrices Oreshkov-Costa-Brukner 2012, Baumann et al. noncausal Page-Wootters circuits 2022, Oreshkov 2019
open_questions: How PM indefinite temporal order relates to formal causal nonseparability (no causal game is analyzed); whether the equivalence of relational-dynamics approaches survives interactions (paper defers to trinity literature); correction: authors and submission date here supersede the earlier frontier-lane record, which mislisted authors as 'Vincent Baumann, Maximilian P. E. Lock' and dated v1 to 2023-11-10
relevance: Anchor 2: defines TO vs PM operational event notions; source of the non-ideal-clock indefinite temporal order result and of the only TO-PM equivalence statement in the comparison set
limits: v1 read, not the 2025 published version (v1 is the only arXiv version); perturbative results not reproduced; no process-matrix formalism used, so its relation to causal nonseparability remains a flagged analogy, not a result

title: Time delocalization and causality across temporal quantum reference frames
version: arXiv:2603.08845v1 (2026-03-09); related DOI 10.1103/9pl6-z9g4 on abs page (journal version not identified; v1 is the only arXiv version)
locators: Sec. II Page-Wootters with reduction maps: R_i(tau_i) Eq. (13), R_i^-1 Eq. (14), frame-change S_i->j(tau_i,tau_j)=R_j(tau_j) R_i^-1(tau_i) Eq. (15), observable transformation O_|Cj = S O_|Ci S^dagger, non-local transformed operations Eqs. (46)-(47); Sec. III no-go on perfect synchronization (delta(0) divergence, Eqs. 21-24); Sec. IV opposing clocks Eqs. (25)-(31) and footnote 3 on thermodynamic arrow; Sec. V operational causality via signaling Eqs. (32)-(36), breakdown of naive embedding Sec. V.2; Sec. VI.1 timed interventions via constraint terms Eq. (48)-(52); Sec. VI.2 constraint class Eq. (57)-(58) and recovered operational probabilities; Sec. VI.3 two-clock cases Eqs. (62)-(74); Sec. VI.4 relational quantum switch Eq. (68) with tau_a=tau_b and bimodal phi(t_2), Eqs. (75) and Fig. 7; Appendix A Eqs. (76)-(79) clock-dependent ordering only for Hermitian dilations; Appendix B two-qubit signaling example Eqs. (80)-(112); Appendix C interaction-picture Dyson method Eqs. (115)-(140)
assumptions: Ideal clocks throughout (unbounded-below spectrum) except Sec. III remark; kinematical Hilbert space with multiple clocks and constraint C=sum H_Ci + H_rest; physical states by group averaging delta(C); frame changes via reduction maps; two approaches to interventions: (i) alternative solutions to one constraint (history choice), (ii) interventions encoded in the constraint operator as f(T_j) tensor K terms, approximately instantaneous (delta(T-tau) notation flagged as abuse, finite-width approximation); necessary time delocalization phi(t_2) between clocks; kinematical states of product form to generate solutions
conclusion: Authors' claims: normalizable physical states forbid perfectly synchronized clocks, so every other clock is necessarily time-delocalized in a given frame (Sec. III); with the naive intervention modeling, operations that are subsystem-local in one clock frame act on all subsystems in another frame (Eqs. 45-47), so causal interpretation fails across frames; encoding interventions in the constraint preserves subsystem-locality across frames while the operation timed by the other clock appears time-delocalized (Fig. 5-6); signaling relations and the probabilities p(b|intervention), p(b|no intervention) are frame-independent (Appendix B); two ideal clocks with opposite signs in the constraint define opposite time directions only approximately, and clock-dependent ordering of two spontaneous operations requires their Stinespring dilations to be time-reversal symmetric, i.e. Hermitian unitaries such as Pauli operators on a qubit (Appendix A); when each clock times one intervention with tau_a=tau_b and a bimodal clock correlation phi(t_2), both orders contribute in both frames, reproducing the causal reference frame decomposition of the quantum switch (Sec. VI.4), and both frames agree that the order is indefinite, 'in keeping with' de la Hamette et al. PRL 2025
proof_status: Full HTML text read at stated locators including Appendices A-C; conditional-evolution case analyses (Eqs. 70, 75) inspected but the case arithmetic not independently re-derived; probabilities recovered symbolically at one point (Appendix B), not numerically reproduced
dependencies: Page-Wootters; Smith-Ahmadi 2019 clock-system interactions; Hoehn-Vanrietvelde 2020 clock switches; Ali Ahmad et al. quantum relativity of subsystems 2022; Castro-Ruiz et al. 2020 temporal localisability; Guerin-Brukner 2018 and Baumann et al. PRR 2022 causal reference frame decomposition; de la Hamette et al. PRL 135, 141402 (2025); Vilasini-Renner 2024 no-go papers
open_questions: Authors': synchronization of many distributed clocks under limited joint localizability; effect of relaxing ideality (their Appendix C method breaks); whether PW equivalence to other relational-dynamics approaches survives clock-system interactions. Ours: no process-matrix analysis is given for the relational switch - whether its correlations are causally nonseparable is unestablished in the paper
relevance: Anchor 3: the direct comparison of frame-relative causal order across temporal QRFs; source of the frame-change map S_i->j, the frame-invariance of signaling, and the both-frames-agree relational quantum switch
limits: Preprint, single version, not yet peer-reviewed at reading time; ideal clocks and approximately instantaneous interventions; the relational switch arises from a chosen physical state (phi(t_2) as control), which the authors themselves contrast with the 'physical' switch of Castro-Ruiz et al. 2020; opposing-clock ordering result is approximate and dilation-restricted

title: Quantum correlations with no causal order
locators: Causal inequality Eqs. (1)-(2) with assumptions CS (causal structure), FC (free choice), CL (closed laboratories); process probability rule Eq. (3); process-matrix conditions Eqs. (4)-(5); causally separable form Eq. (6); example process Eq. (7); violation Eq. (8) p_succ=(2+sqrt2)/4; Appendix .1 formal derivation Eqs. (9)-(11); Appendix .2 definition Eqs. (12)-(15); Appendix .3 Hilbert-Schmidt characterization (allowed term types, general W); Appendix .5 protocol Eqs. (20)-(27); Appendix .6 classical processes causally separable Eqs. (28)-(32)
assumptions: Only local validity of quantum mechanics: each party performs quantum instruments on a system passing once through a closed laboratory; probabilities bilinear in CP maps (derived from randomization and coarse-graining); free random bits; no global causal structure assumed; noncontextuality of joint probabilities assumed
conclusion: Established (peer-reviewed) results: all bipartite probabilities compatible with local QM are Tr[W(M_i x M_j)] with W positive semidefinite and normalized on all CPTP pairs; definite-order scenarios and probabilistic mixtures thereof are causally separable W = q W^{B not-preceq A} + (1-q) W^{A not-preceq B}; a specific four-qubit W (Eq. 7) satisfies the process conditions but is not causally separable and yields p_succ=(2+sqrt2)/4 > 3/4 for the communication game; all classical (pointer-basis diagonal) processes are causally separable; any process matrix can be read as a CPTP map from outputs to inputs (noisy backward-in-time channel), so no logical paradox arises
proof_status: Full HTML text read including all six appendix sections; derivations followed symbolically; the example-process inequality computation (Eqs. 24-27) read in detail, not independently recomputed; published version is the peer-reviewed record
dependencies: Choi-Jamio lkowski isomorphism; quantum instruments; quantum combs (Chiribella et al.) for the equivalent normalization conditions; CHSH analogy noted by authors
open_questions: Authors': maximal quantum violation of the causal inequality was open in 2012 (later literature not audited here); realization beyond optical switches unaddressed. Ours: the framework contains no transformations between perspectives, which is exactly the structural contrast with the QRF anchors
relevance: Anchor 5 (process-matrix baseline): defines process-matrix indefinite order operationally (causal nonseparability certified by the causal inequality), the fixed point against which frame-relative order notions are contrasted
limits: Bipartite case only, two parties each with qubit input/output in the example; no spacetime or frame notions appear, so any bridging to QRF frames is interpretive; later refinements (causally nonseparable but inequality-satisfying processes such as the quantum switch) come from follow-up literature not audited at full text here
